title: The explicit glued integral module
statement: Let X be a scheme, J its pro-etale topology, R and S sheaves of commutative rings on J, a : R → S a ring-sheaf morphism, and L an S-module sheaf. An integral lattice pair on U consists of a finite locally free R|U-module P and a specified isomorphism S|U ⊗ P ≅ L|U, with the sheafified tensor product. Suppose the coefficient map is injective on every slice test object. Let r be a covering sieve on U and x a compatible family of represented lattice image families along r. Choose actual representatives of these given classes. Their embeddings have equal ranges on all overlap tests; composing the linear equivalences to their common range gives explicit transitions. The sheaf of all-test-object tuples compatible with restriction and these transitions is a finite locally free R|U-module. Its restrictions to covering objects are canonically isomorphic to the chosen local modules. [lem-weil-pbc-lattice-class-presheaf, def-weil-pbc-site-module-compatible-tuples, lem-weil-pbc-site-module-compatible-tuples].

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(6), pp. 59–60; Descent and an exact presentation of lattice classes

proof.text: Choose representatives of the actual given image classes. Injective embeddings with equal ranges give transitions via linear equivalences to their common range. Injectivity proves naturality and cocycles. Use the compatible-tuple sheaf and local isomorphisms. Refine the original cover by local finite free basis covers, transporting free modules along iterated-slice equivalences.
